text: PRE-REGISTERED (plan 0b098bfae805). The SAME 14 affinity predictions from study v1, re-scored against references that are medians over ALL ChEMBL records rather than whichever single record a flat activity budget captured. Median records per compound rose from effectively 1 to 4.5.

H2 FALSIFIED, AND IT REFUTES MY OWN HYPOTHESIS. I predicted that reference quality was study v1's binding limit and that fixing it would raise the correlation. Spearman rho went DOWN, from 0.304 to 0.1912 (change -0.1128), with a 95% CI of [-0.4622, 0.7303] that spans zero. The references were not the problem. My earlier statement that about 40% of the headline discrepancy was a reference artefact holds for huperzine A specifically (2.41 -> 1.44 log) but does NOT generalise: the overall ranking did not improve.

H3 CONFIRMED and this is the operative result. The model's median absolute error is 1.0471 log10 while the references' own median dispersion across independent assays is 0.4445 log10. The model is the larger error term by roughly 2.4x, so it is the term worth improving. Study v1 could only cite a literature noise floor (Kalliokoski's 0.68); this measures the floor in situ on the same compounds and shows the model exceeds it.

MEASURED LITERATURE DISPERSION, which is worth recording on its own. Complete retrieval shows donepezil x AChE has 176 ChEMBL records spanning 5.00 log10 units — the published IC50 for a marketed drug against its primary target disagrees by five orders of magnitude. Tacrine has 201 records spanning 2.57, physostigmine 55 spanning 4.76, huperzine A 25 spanning 3.99. Any single-record reference for these compounds is close to arbitrary.

TOOLING. corpus.all_activities / reference_potency now retrieve every record for a compound-target pair via the ChEMBL Elasticsearch backend, discarding inequality-qualified values because a bound is not a measurement. The public REST endpoint returned HTTP 500 throughout this work, which is why the ES backend is used directly.
